clue: Temporary cessation of breathing
Absence of urine output, typically under 100 mL in 24 hours
Black, tarry, foul-smelling stool from digested blood, classically indicating an upper GI bleed
A concentrated dose of medication or fluid given rapidly, often IV
Painful or difficult urination
Abnormal fluid buildup in the peritoneal cavity
A clot or other mass that travels through the bloodstream
Excessive urine production
Elevated nitrogenous waste products, like BUN, in the blood
A blood clot that forms and stays at its site of origin
High-pitched breath sound caused by narrowed airways
Breathing difficulty when lying flat, relieved by sitting up
Low oxygen level in the arterial blood
Hives; raised, itchy welts from histamine release, allergic or not
Tiny pinpoint spots from minor hemorrhage under the skin
Excessive thirst
Coughing up blood from the lungs or airway
A medication given to prevent or treat nausea and vomiting
Elevated level of potassium in the blood
Abnormally low neutrophil count that raises infection risk
